question.prompt: For distinct real numbers \(x\) and \(y,\) let \(M(x,y)\) be the larger of \(x\) and \(y\) and let \(m(x,y)\) be the smaller of \(x\) and \(y.\) If \[ a\lt b\lt c\lt d\lt e, \] then \[ \begin{aligned} &M\bigl(M(a,m(b,c)),\\ &\qquad m(d,m(a,e))\bigr)= \end{aligned} \]

solutions.explanation:
Use the given order to evaluate the innermost selections first. Since \(b<c\) and \(a<e\),
\[
m(b,c)=b,\qquad m(a,e)=a.
\]
The two arguments of the outer \(M\) therefore become
\[
M(a,b)=b,\qquad m(d,a)=a.
\]
Finally, since \(a<b\), the whole expression is \(M(b,a)=b\). All compared arguments are distinct, as required by the definitions. The answer is \(\boxed{b}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Evaluate from the inside outward
